yield_token.notes: transfer fetches the exchange rate once and shares it across the sender/recipient accrue_yield pair; unhinted it walked YT -> YM -> vault -> Blend twice for a value that cannot change within a transaction. Also: burn_with_rate / transfer_with_rate are admin-gated only.

yield_manager.notes: Flash callbacks take the vault rate as an argument instead of re-reading it. update_exchange_rate is split: the vault read is separable from the policy (non-decreasing floor, maturity lock, storage write), which all stays in the YM. This is what brought zap_asset_for_yt inside the budget. MUST be deployed together with amm b079327d - the callback ABI changed.

amm.notes: Passes its already-loaded VaultRate into the flash callbacks so the receiver need not repeat the read. Keeps reading the vault directly for its own pricing - the value flows from the contract that read the vault to the one applying policy on it, never the reverse. MUST be deployed together with yield_manager ceff0ceb - the callback ABI changed.

router.notes: Expired exit reordered so the LP withdrawal and yield claim land before a single YM redemption; duplicate balance and query_asset reads removed.

blend_vault.notes: Adds query_asset and redeem; fixes withdraw authorization. get_signer is null, so deposits are permissionless.

fee_config.note: 1e7-scaled fraction OF each trade's fee (10%), not of trade volume. Snapshotted into each market at creation; set_fee_config is prospective only.

router.notes: No upgrade entrypoint, so a new address each time - cheap, since the router custodies nothing and holds no approvals.

markets.notes: STALE. Created 2026-07-27T21:42, two minutes after the new AMM was installed but two days BEFORE yt 18bcafd9 / ym 067d8228. Markets are immutable, so it is frozen on the pre-fix YT (which looked the rate up twice per transfer) and a YM that does not expose exit_expired_to_asset at all. Both YT zaps exceed budget here; exit_expired_to_asset will fail as an unknown function when this market matures 2026-09-16. Share-denominated exit_expired still works. This market is what every 'YT zaps are structurally impossible' measurement was taken against - see docs/YT_ZAP_BUDGET.md.

Diagnostic baseline, pre-R2. Created to isolate stale WASM from the budget problem: on this market zap_yt_for_asset SUCCEEDS (31,462,249 instr) where it fails on the 1789517001 market, proving that failure was stale bytecode rather than anything structural. zap_asset_for_yt still exceeded here, which is what R2 then fixed. Kept for comparison; superseded by 1817200000. Pool seeded 1e9 PT / 6.24e8 V.

First market on the R2 contracts. EVERY zap simulates within budget here, including zap_asset_for_yt (32,136,043 instr), which no earlier market could execute. Pool seeded 1e9 PT / 6.24e8 V, matching 1817100000 so the two are directly comparable. Post-maturity paths (exit_expired, exit_expired_to_asset) are NOT verified - this market matures 2027.
Pre-rate-caching AMM. Verified here: the full 100 XLM split round trip, zap_asset_for_pt, zap_pt_for_asset, zap_lp_for_asset. zap_asset_for_lp exceeded budget on this AMM.

stale_markets.note: Created before the signature-drift rework. They function for share-denominated operations but their zaps cannot be signed: the YT they carry demands the holder's signature over a live exchange rate, and their AMM prices the amount a user must pre-authorize. Markets are immutable, so these are abandoned rather than fixed.

superseded.note: The 2026-07-18 deployment is abandoned, not migrated. Its markets point at the old Blend vault, carry the pre-fix yield token (self-transfer minted YT), and none of PT/YT/YM/AMM/router expose an upgrade entrypoint. The old factory could not be upgraded either: its constructor gained FeeConfig, and upgrade does not re-run a constructor, so get_fee_config would panic on unset storage.

budget_findings.measured_on: market 1817200000 (R2 contracts), pool seeded 1e9 PT / 6.24e8 V, 10-unit trades
budget_findings.note: No zap exceeds budget any more. The earlier 'the two YT zaps are structurally impossible' finding was wrong on two counts: it was measured against market 1789517001, which is frozen on pre-fix YT/YM bytecode, and it reasoned from CPU when the binding limit is memory. Every path above sits at 13-32% of the 100M instruction limit, so instruction percentage is NOT headroom - zap_asset_for_yt failed at an estimated ~36% before R2. See docs/YT_ZAP_BUDGET.md.
budget_findings.unverified_note: Both expired-exit paths revert on the maturity assert on every current market (all mature 2027+), so neither has ever run on R2 contracts. exit_expired_to_asset is the heaviest path in the system. The factory only enforces maturity > now, so a market dated ~10 minutes out would close this gap cheaply.
budget_findings.exit_expired_caveat: Converts the caller ENTIRE vault-share balance up to sweep_allowance, not just what the call produced - the YM authenticates from, so its figure must be a pre-signed ceiling. Observed live sweeping unrelated leftover shares. Size sweep_allowance to the expected proceeds.
budget_findings.abi_coupling: amm b079327d and yield_manager ceff0ceb changed the flash-callback ABI together and are NOT interchangeable with their predecessors. Installing one without the other produces markets whose flash swaps fail. Verify factory.get_wasm_hashes() before create_market.
